relationships.subject: STN–LPB neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: These data support the notion that stimulation of STN–LPB neurons induces mechanical hypersensitivity in naïve mice.

relationships.subject: STN–LPB neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: In persistent pain states, such as CFA-induced inflammatory pain (Fig. 4j, k; Supplementary Fig. 4c) and SNI-induced neuropathic pain (Fig. 4l–n), we also observed that optogenetic silencing of STN–LPB neurons reduced mechanical and thermal hypersensitivity of the contralateral hind paw.

relationships.subject: STN glutamatergic neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: These experiments demonstrate that optogenetic stimulation of STN glutamatergic terminals is sufficient to increase the activity of LPB neurons.

relationships.subject: STN–LPB projection
relationships.evidence_quote: Similarly, contralateral capsaicin-, CFA-, and SNI-induced pain-like hypersensitivity in the hind paw were attenuated by optogenetic silencing of the STN–LPB projection

relationships.subject: STN–LPB projection
relationships.evidence_quote: Consistent with this, SNI-induced increase in c-Fos expression in the LPB was markedly reduced by optogenetic silencing of the STN–LPB projection

relationships.subject: SNr GABAergic neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: This enhancement was accompanied by hypoactivity in SNr<sup>GABA</sup> neurons and strengthening of the STN-LPB glutamatergic projection.

key_findings: STN neurons are hyperactive in capsaicin, CFA and SNI pain states and directly excite LPB glutamatergic neurons.

Optogenetic silencing of STN–LPB neurons or their LPB projection attenuated acute and persistent pain-like hypersensitivity in male and female mice, while activation induced hypersensitivity in naive mice.
